contract.name: skills-contract
consumers: NERVIS 0.32.0: the Skills page and NERVIS chat
Clarvis's own engine: a later build, in the Clarvis repository

about: Skills for every engine (owner decisions, 15 September 2026): the Skills page's list and switches, and the reads of the models that aren't Codex. RAVIS owns this file in ravis/tests/fixtures/relay-contract/; Clarvis keeps a byte-identical copy in src/test/fixtures/, held to codex-contract.sha256. Every path, name and text is a fixture value.
decisions: Besides Codex, skills are for Clarvis's own engine and NERVIS chat, together called the other models (engine models).
Each skill has one switch for Codex and one for the other models, so it can be on for one and off for the other.
The NERVIS skills folder's skills start on for both engines. The owner's personal skills start off for both, and so does any added later. Codex's built-in skills exist only for Codex.
A skill is trusted content the owner chose, and only a skill switched on is ever served.
access: GET /api/v1/skills takes NERVIS's client credential (its GET relay) or an admin credential. POST /api/v1/skills takes an admin credential: NERVIS's Skills page, through its control route. GET /api/v1/skills/models and GET /api/v1/skills/models/read take Clarvis's client credential (an application in settings.agent_client_applications) or NERVIS's, and refuse anonymous callers, admin credentials and every other client. Each refusal is 403 FORBIDDEN. This is UX and audit, not a boundary against local programs.
older_forms: GET and POST /api/v1/codex/skills (codex-admin.json) are the older form of GET and POST /api/v1/skills, for Codex alone. They answer exactly as they did, for NERVIS 0.31, and a Codex switch through either is the same choice.

skills.what: a folder holding a SKILL.md: YAML front matter with name and description, then the instructions, and perhaps other files the instructions point at

sources.nervis: the NERVIS skills folder, settings.codex_skills_folder (<NERVIS workspace>/clarvis/skills)
sources.built_in: Codex's built-in skills, as Codex's own skills/list gives them; Codex's only

reading: a skill is a folder at most four folders below its source's root holding a SKILL.md; hidden folders are skipped, and a skill's own sub-folders aren't searched for more
a link is followed only when its real path stays inside that root; a link leading out to a skill is listed with that problem and never read
SKILL.md, and any file served, is at most 64 KB of UTF-8 text
a skill without front matter, with YAML that doesn't parse, or without a name or a description is listed with its problem and never served
each skill once, by the real path of its SKILL.md, the NERVIS folder's first; a read stops at 200 skills or 2000 folders per root and says so
skills.id: <source>/<the skill's folder relative to its root>, e.g. nervis/nervis-notes: stable while the folder keeps its name and place, and never a full path
skills.lined_up_with_codex: a skill Codex lists and a skill RAVIS read are one skill when the real path of Codex's path is the real path of RAVIS's SKILL.md, links followed on both sides

for_models.mechanism: progressive disclosure, as Codex uses skills: a short list in the model's instructions, and a skill's full text only when it fits
steps: Before a model request, read GET /api/v1/skills/models. When it lists no skill, add nothing to the model's instructions.
Otherwise add a short list to the instructions: one line per skill with its name, description and id.

Read a skill's SKILL.md, or a file it names, with GET /api/v1/skills/models/read only when that skill fits: through a tool the model can call with the id and a path relative to the skill's folder, or, for a caller without tools, by choosing the fitting skill before the request, as NERVIS chat does.
Hand the text to the model marked as the owner's skill, after the program's own rules.
for_models.precedence: A skill never overrides the calling program's own safety rules, approvals or tool limits. Say so in the instructions, with the program's rules first.
for_models.when_a_change_counts: RAVIS reads the folders and the owner's switches on every call, so read the list for each model request and keep no skill text beyond the request that read it: a change counts from the other models' next request.
for_models.a_refused_read: SKILL_NOT_FOUND (switched off since the list was read), SKILL_FILE_REFUSED or SKILL_FILE_NOT_FOUND is told to the model plainly, and the request carries on without that text.

routes.needs: NERVIS's client credential (its GET relay) or an admin credential; never Clarvis
routes.answer: SkillsBoard {folders: {nervis, personal: {path, problem}}, codex: {listed, problem}, skills: [{id, name, description, source, path, problem, codex: {available, enabled}, models: {available, enabled}}]}
rules: folders.<source>.path is that folder as a real path; problem is null, or why its skills aren't all listed: its setting can't be used, it can't be read, or the read stopped at a limit. A folder that isn't there yet lists nothing, with no problem
skills lists every skill RAVIS read in those folders and every skill Codex lists but a project's own, each once, lined up by real path, grouped nervis, personal, built_in and by name within each

id is <source>/<folder relative to its root> for a skill RAVIS read, and <source>/<folder name> for one only Codex lists, with ~2, ~3 added when two would be the same; path is the real path of RAVIS's SKILL.md, or Codex's path for a skill only Codex lists
description is one line of at most 300 characters; problem is null, or why the other models can't use a skill RAVIS couldn't read whole, in plain words

codex.available: Codex lists the skill just now; codex.enabled: Codex's own answer. codex.listed is false while Codex can't say which skills it has: codex.problem then says why, no skill has a Codex switch, and built-in skills aren't listed. Otherwise codex.problem is the sentence GET /api/v1/codex gives while the owner's choices can't be applied, or null
models.available: RAVIS read the skill whole, so never a built-in skill or one only Codex lists; models.enabled: served to the other models now
a skill the owner never switched is on for both engines when nervis and off for both when personal, one added later included; built_in is on for Codex
read from disk, the owner's switches and Codex on every call, never kept

routes.body: {path, engine, enabled}: a skill's path exactly as GET listed it; codex or models; true or false
rules: a body without a path of 1 to 4096 characters, an engine of codex or models, and a boolean enabled is 422 INVALID_REQUEST_BODY

engine models: only the path of a skill RAVIS read whole just now. A built-in skill, one only Codex lists, one with a problem, or any other path is 404 SKILL_NOT_FOUND {engine} and nothing is kept. The choice is kept at once, by that real path, and counts from the other models' next request; Codex is never asked anything

engine codex: only the path of a skill Codex lists just now (503 CODEX_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE while Codex can't list them; 404 SKILL_NOT_FOUND {engine} for any other path), switched exactly as POST /api/v1/codex/skills switches it: kept by the path Codex lists and applied until skills/list agrees, and 409 SKILL_NOT_CHANGED {skill, reason} with the previous choice put back when Codex doesn't take it. It counts from a Codex task's next start or reopen
one engine's switch never changes the other's
switching a skill to what it already is changes nothing, so a retry is safe and no Idempotency-Key is needed
audited as ravis.skill_switched {name, source, engine, enabled} once kept, and for codex once Codex took it

routes.needs: Clarvis's client credential or NERVIS's: the programs calling the models that aren't Codex; never an admin credential
routes.query: skill: an id from GET /api/v1/skills/models; file: a path inside the skill's folder, relative and / separated, SKILL.md when left out
routes.answer: {skill, name, file, bytes, text}: the file as UTF-8 text, a SKILL.md's front matter included
rules: only a skill switched on for the other models just now and read whole: any other skill, switched off, unknown or with a problem alike, is 404 SKILL_NOT_FOUND, so a caller learns nothing about the skills it may not read

file must name a regular file inside the skill's own folder, links followed: an absolute path, an empty, . or .. part, a backslash, a control character, or a link leading out of the folder is 422 SKILL_FILE_REFUSED {reason: outside_skill}; a hidden part, as asked or where a link leads, is hidden; over 64 KB is too_large; not UTF-8 is not_text
no file there, a folder, or a file RAVIS may not read is 404 SKILL_FILE_NOT_FOUND
logged with the caller's application, the skill's id, the file's path and its size, refusals too; never what the file says

body.name: nervis-notes
body.text:
---
name: nervis-notes
description: How NERVIS tasks keep their notes.
---

# Keeping notes

Keep a task's notes in NOTES.md at the project's root, newest first.
For the layout, read references/guide.md.

body.name: nervis-notes
body.text:
# The notes guide

One heading per day, and one line per finding under it.

nervis_control_routes.rule: checks NERVIS's control token (header x-nervis-control), then calls RAVIS with NERVIS's RAVIS admin credential (admin.launcher)

routes.ravis: POST /api/v1/skills (NERVIS 0.32.0; forwards only path, engine and enabled)

nervis_control_routes.never: no NERVIS route forwards to the other models' routes: NERVIS chat reads them itself with NERVIS's client credential, and the Skills page reads GET /api/v1/skills through the existing GET relay
